title: VAPT Auto-Heal Implementation Contract v1.0
description: Machine-readable contract governing the implementation of auto-heal capabilities across all VAPT bundle files. This contract defines the phased execution plan, per-phase actions, validation gates, and sign-off criteria to bring auto-heal coverage from 27.3% (117/429 steps) to near-complete. It is loaded by the AI Agent at runtime and enforced as a hard constraint on all auto-heal implementation tasks. This contract extends (not replaces) vapt_platform_contract_v3.0.json.

stakeholder_context.objective: Implement a complete auto-heal mechanism where enabling a feature auto-injects protection into configuration files, and disabling it auto-removes that protection — reliably, idempotently, and with verification

auto_heal_definition.enable_flow: Feature ON → Check idempotency → Backup → Inject wrapped_code (with markers) at insertion_point → Verify injection → On failure, auto-rollback
auto_heal_definition.disable_flow: Feature OFF → Locate begin_marker in target_file → Regex-remove marker block → Verify removal → On failure, restore from backup
auto_heal_definition.core_principle: Every protection that can be injected MUST be removable by a corresponding, symmetric, marker-based operation — no orphaned code, no partial states

target_state.remaining_gap: Cloudflare API rollback requires new action type (design-only in this contract)

structural_preservation_rule.description: The JSON schema/structure of all existing bundle files is IMMUTABLE. Auto-heal implementation may only add key-value pairs within the existing structure — never change the structure itself.
rules: Top-level keys must NEVER be renamed, removed, or reordered
The nesting hierarchy must remain identical — new fields are added as siblings at the appropriate level
Value types must be preserved — strings stay strings, objects stay objects, arrays stay arrays
New fields (e.g., disable_action, remove_operation, marker_begin, marker_end) must follow the naming conventions already established in each file
New rollback{} objects in driver manifest must follow the exact same key structure as existing rollback objects: {action, begin_marker, end_marker, target_file}
New disable actions in interface schema must follow the exact same key structure as existing enable actions: {action_id, type, label, confirmation_required, rest_endpoint}
The contract file (vapt_autoheal_contract_v1.0.json) is a NEW file with its own independent structure and is not bound by this rule
JSON formatting style (indentation, key ordering conventions) must match the source files

marker_system_reference.description: The marker system is the foundation of auto-heal. Every injected protection block is wrapped in platform-appropriate comment markers for reliable identification and removal.

cloudflare.note: Cloudflare uses API-based rule management, not file markers. Rollback requires DELETE API call.

marker_system_reference.wordpress_convention_alignment: Mirrors WordPress core # BEGIN WordPress / # END WordPress pattern

phase_1.title: Critical Bug Fix — LiteSpeed Rollback Action Missing
phase_1.description: All 8 litespeed enforcer steps in vapt_driver_manifest_v2.0.json have rollback objects with begin_marker and end_marker, but the 'action' key is completely absent. This is a bug (likely from remediation) that prevents programmatic rollback execution. Fix: add action: 'remove_block' to all 8 rollback objects.

actions.description: For each of the 8 litespeed steps, locate the rollback object and add the missing 'action' key with value 'remove_block'
actions.position_rule: Insert 'action' as the FIRST key in the rollback object (consistent with existing .htaccess rollback objects)

actions.description: Verify that the same 8 litespeed steps in enforcer_pattern_library_v2.0.json have rollback fields (even if string-only). If missing, add rollback string.
actions.check: For each litespeed enforcer in pattern library, verify 'rollback' key exists. If missing, add string: 'Remove # BEGIN VAPT RISK-XXX ... # END VAPT RISK-XXX block from .htaccess'

validation_gates.description: All 8 litespeed rollback objects in driver manifest must have action='remove_block'
validation_gates.check: For each risk in affected_risks, find litespeed step in vapt_driver_manifest and verify step.rollback.action === 'remove_block'

validation_gates.description: No litespeed rollback object may have action=null or action missing
validation_gates.check: For each litespeed step, verify step.rollback.action is not null and is not undefined

validation_gates.check: For each litespeed step, verify step.rollback.begin_marker === step.begin_marker AND step.rollback.end_marker === step.end_marker

phase_1.risk_level: LOW — additive field only, no structural change

phase_2.title: Rollback Gap Closure — Generate 312 Missing Rollback Objects
phase_2.description: 312 driver manifest steps have begin_marker, end_marker, and target_file but are missing the rollback{} object. Since all infrastructure is present, rollback objects can be generated deterministically using a template. This phase brings rollback coverage from 27.3% (117/429) to 99.5% (429/429 excluding Cloudflare).

phase_3.title: Interface Schema Enable/Disable Parity
phase_3.description: The interface_schema currently defines 133 enable actions and ZERO disable actions. This makes the toggle UI a one-way street — it can turn protections ON but has no schema-defined path to turn them OFF. This phase adds a disable action for every risk and extends toggle components with on_enable/on_disable callback semantics.

actions.description: Add a 'disable' action to every risk's actions[] array
actions.position_rule: Insert as the second element in the actions[] array, after the existing enable action

actions.description: Extend every toggle component with on_enable and on_disable callback references
actions.note: The existing on_change handler remains for backward compatibility. The new on_enable/on_disable handlers provide explicit enable/disable callback paths. The plugin code should call on_enable when toggle transitions to true and on_disable when it transitions to false.

actions.position_rule: Add immediately after the existing 'operation' field in each platform_implementations entry

actions.description: Add 'marker_begin' and 'marker_end' fields to every platform_implementations entry (except cloudflare which is API-based)
actions.position_rule: Add after remove_operation field in each platform_implementations entry

actions.description: Add 'disable_driver_ref' field to every platform_implementations entry

phase_4.title: Pattern Library Rollback Structuring
phase_4.description: The enforcer_pattern_library currently has rollback as a human-readable string (e.g., 'Remove # BEGIN VAPT RISK-002 ... # END VAPT RISK-002 block from .htaccess'). While the driver manifest has structured rollback objects, the pattern library's string-only rollback cannot be programmatically consumed. This phase adds a structured rollback_object alongside the existing string rollback (not replacing it — to preserve backward compatibility and the structural preservation rule).

actions.description: Add 'rollback_structured' object to every enforcer entry that has markers
actions.position_rule: Add immediately after the existing 'rollback' string field
actions.count: approximately 398 (one per enforcer entry with markers)
actions.note: Cloudflare entries (no markers) get rollback_structured with action='delete_waf_rule' and null markers

actions.description: Add 'remove_mode' field to every driver{} sub-object
actions.position_rule: Add after 'if_found' field in the driver{} sub-object
actions.note: This provides the driver with a symmetric remove instruction, complementing the existing write_mode

phase_5.title: Post-Removal Verification
phase_5.description: Currently, verification only exists for the ENABLE path (after injecting code). When a feature is DISABLED, there is no verification that the block was successfully removed. This phase adds 'disable_verification' fields to the driver manifest for every step, enabling the driver to confirm removal succeeded.

actions.description: Add 'disable_verification' object to every step that has a rollback object

description_of_fields.check_type: How to verify removal — 'marker_absent' means scan the file for the begin_marker; if not found, removal succeeded
description_of_fields.check_string: The string to search for — typically the begin_marker
description_of_fields.expected_result: What we expect — 'not_found' means the marker is absent from the file
description_of_fields.fallback_verification: Optional additional verification (e.g., check site still loads, check header is no longer present). Null for most entries; populated for header-related risks.

actions.position_rule: Add immediately after the rollback object in each step
actions.count: approximately 429 (one per step, after Phase 2 ensures all have rollback)

actions.description: For header-related risks (RISK-012 through RISK-022, RISK-024, RISK-031-033, RISK-134), add fallback_verification that confirms the header is no longer present

validation_gates.description: Every step with rollback must have disable_verification
validation_gates.check: For each step, verify disable_verification object exists

validation_gates.description: disable_verification must have check_type, check_string, expected_result
validation_gates.check: Verify all 3 required keys exist and are non-null

validation_gates.description: check_string must match the step's begin_marker
validation_gates.check: disable_verification.check_string === step.begin_marker

phase_6.title: Cloudflare API Rollback Design
phase_6.description: Cloudflare is API-based (WAF custom rules, transform rules) and does not use file markers. Rollback requires a different mechanism — deleting the rule via Cloudflare API. This phase defines the schema for Cloudflare rollback but notes that actual implementation requires Cloudflare API credentials and rule IDs that are only available at runtime. The contract defines the structure; the PHP driver code would need to implement the API calls.

actions.description: Add rollback objects to all 32 Cloudflare steps in driver manifest with API-based action type
actions.note: rule_identifier must reference a field in the step that uniquely identifies the WAF rule. The zone_id and ruleset_id are runtime values. The contract defines the structure; actual values are populated at runtime by the PHP driver.

actions.description: Add rollback_structured objects to all 32 Cloudflare entries in enforcer pattern library

rollback_structured.note: Cloudflare rollback requires API call. File-marker-based removal does not apply.

global_validation_gates.description: These gates apply across ALL phases and must be checked after each phase completes.

gates.name: Structural Preservation
gates.description: No existing top-level keys renamed, removed, or reordered. No nesting hierarchy changes. No value type changes.

gates.name: No Orphaned References
gates.description: Every new field that references another file must resolve to an existing entry.

gates.name: Platform Scope Compliance
gates.description: No IIS, Caddy, fail2ban references introduced or re-introduced by auto-heal additions.

gates.name: Marker Consistency
gates.description: Markers for the same risk+enforcer pair must be identical across all files that reference them.

gates.name: JSON Validity
gates.description: All modified files must be valid JSON (parseable without errors).

execution_order.description: Phases MUST be executed in order. Each phase's validation gates must pass before proceeding to the next phase.
execution_order.rollback_on_failure: If any phase fails validation, STOP execution. Do NOT proceed to the next phase. Report the failing gate and wait for human decision.
execution_order.checkpoint_action: After each phase completes and passes validation, save a snapshot of all modified files to /home/z/my-project/download/checkpoints/phase_{N}/

sign_off_criteria.description: The auto-heal implementation is complete when ALL of the following are true:
criteria: All 8 phases executed in order with all validation gates passing
Rollback coverage >= 99% for file-writing enforcers (429/429 for file-based, 32/32 for Cloudflare API)
All 133 risks have both enable and disable actions
All 429 driver manifest steps have rollback objects
All 398 enforcer pattern library entries have rollback_structured objects
All interface schema platform_implementations have remove_operation and marker fields
Zero prohibited platform references (IIS, Caddy, fail2ban) in any file

contract_enforcement.agent_instruction: BEFORE implementing any auto-heal changes, load this contract AND vapt_platform_contract_v3.0.json. Execute phases strictly in order. After each phase, run that phase's validation gates AND the global validation gates. If any CRITICAL gate fails, STOP and report. Do not proceed to the next phase until all gates pass. This contract extends (not replaces) the platform contract — both must be satisfied simultaneously.
contract_enforcement.checkpoint_protocol: After each phase, write a summary to /home/z/my-project/worklog.md with: phase_id, actions completed, validation results, any issues encountered. This provides a full audit trail.

estimated_totals.highest_risk_phase: AH-P3 (Interface Schema — large number of additions per risk)
